703849.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dúwo, from Proto-Indo-European *duwó, a variant of *dwóh₁. Cognates include Sanskrit द्व (dvá), Old Armenian երկու (erku), Latin duo, and Old English twā (English two).

703887.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dwoΗdeḱm̥. Cognates include Sanskrit द्वादश (dvā́daśa) and Latin duodecim.

703833.t: From Proto-Indo-European *drem- (“to run”) + -ος (-os); cognate with Sanskrit द्राति (drā́ti, “to run”), द्रम् (drámati, “to run”); Proto-Germanic *tradō (“way, track, spoor”).

703817.t: Related to Mycenaean Greek 𐀈𐀁𐀫 (do-e-ro /⁠dohelos⁠/), possibly from Canaanite *dōʾēlu “servant, attendant” (compare Late Babylonian 𒁕𒀝𒂵𒇻 (daggālu, “subject, one who waits on another, does their bidding”).

703845.t: From δύναμαι (dúnamai, “to be able”) + -τός (-tós, verbal adjective suffix).

703822.t: Traditionally related to δέρκομαι (dérkomai, “to see”) with the literal meaning of “one who stares” or, alternatively, “sharp-sighted”.

703860.t: Apparently a formation from δυσ- (dus-, “bad, hard, unfortunate”) + a component κόλος (kólos) of unknown meaning and origin, though it could possibly be a variant of χολή (kholḗ, “bile”).

703837.t: From oblique case forms with *drew-, a stem of Proto-Indo-European *dóru (“tree”) (whence also δόρυ (dórŭ)).

703804.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dóru, from Proto-Indo-European *dóru. Cognates include Sanskrit दारु॑ (dā́ru), Old Persian 𐎭𐎠𐎽𐎢𐎺 (d-a-ru-u-v /⁠dāruv⁠/) and Old English trēow (English tree).

703821.t: From the root of δέρκομαι (dérkomai, “I see”), possibly reflecting a thematicized Proto-Indo-European root noun *dérḱs ~ *dr̥ḱós; compare Proto-Celtic *derkos (“eye”). Ultimately from the root *derḱ- (“to see”).

703827.t: Typically derived as a verbal noun (“holding”) of δράσσομαι (drắssomai, “to hold, to seize”).

703801.t: Uncertain. Compare Cornish yorch, Welsh iwrch, which leads to a Proto-Indo-European *yorkos (“roe deer”).

703836.t: From Proto-Hellenic *drumós, Proto-Indo-European *drumós, from the same root as of δόρυ (dóru, “tree”), δρῦς (drûs, “oak”), and δροόν (droón, “strong”). The length of the vowel υ (ū) is taken analogically from δρῦς (drûs).

703828.t: Uncertain. Beekes mentions a connection with Lithuanian darýti (“to make; to do”).

703809.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dótis, from Proto-Indo-European *déh₃tis. By surface analysis, δίδωμι (dídōmi, “to give”) + -σις (-sis, verbal noun suffix).

703856.t: From δύω (dúō, “to cause to sink, plunge”) + -σις (-sĭs).

703838.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dunamai, from a nasal-infixed form of Proto-Indo-European *dewh₂- (“to fit together”).

703825.t: Uncertain. Perhaps related to διδράσκω (didráskō, “to run”) and suffixed with -της (-tēs, masculine agentive suffix), though the origin of the sequence -πέ- (-pé-) is unclear.

703844.t: From δύναμαι (dúnamai, “be able”) + -στης (-stēs, masculine agentive suffix).

703896.t: Reanalyzed as a -μα-stem from Epic δῶ (dô), from Proto-Indo-European *dṓm (“home; house”). Compare δόμος (dómos), δεσπότης (despótēs).

703863.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dusmenḗs, from Proto-Indo-European *dusmenēs (whence also Sanskrit दुर्मनस् (durmanas), Avestan 𐬛𐬎𐬱𐬨𐬀𐬥𐬀𐬵 (dušmanah), Middle Persian [script needed] (dwšmn'), Middle Persian [script needed] (dwšmyn'), Manichaean Middle Persian 𐫅𐫇𐫢𐫖𐫏𐫗…

703807.t: δόρυ (dórŭ, “spear, lance”) + φέρω (phérō, “bear, bring, carry”) + -ος (-os, suffix forming two-termination second-declension compound adjectives)

703835.t: According to Beekes, from Pre-Greek, due to the presence of an intervocalic -σ- (-s-).

703824.t: Retrograde formation from δράσσομαι (drássomai, “to grasp, take handfuls”), which is from Proto-Indo-European *dregʰ-.

703826.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dregʰ-. The LIV suggests either *dr-n̥-gʰ-yé-ti or *dr̥gʰ-yé-ti as the possible pre-forms.

703865.t: From δύω (dúō, “to cause to sink; to plunge”).

703830.t: From reanalysis of older δρεπάνη f (drepắnē) as neuter, originally formed as δρέπω (drépō, “to pluck; to cut off”) + -άνη (-ắnē, instrument noun suffix).

703811.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dh₃tós (“given”). By surface analysis, the root of δίδωμι (dídōmi) + -τός (-tós).
